title: To the church at Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1–17)
hookLine: a messy church split into fan clubs: I follow Paul, I Apollos
tomorrow: why would Paul admit his message sounds foolish?

lines: TEAM THIS ONE, TEAM THAT ONE.
I AM OF PAUL, I OF APOLLOS.
cards: Teams pick favorite coaches. Group chats split over who's right. Acts is done, and the letters begin with a church doing exactly that.

Word reaches Paul from Chloe's people that Corinth is quarreling: "Every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ." Fan clubs. So whose club does Paul go after first?

teach.b: Today's question: what holds a group together when people love different leaders? Paul starts by calling this quarreling church "the church of God which is at Corinth" and its people saints.
Then the plea: "that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you".
Then three questions: "Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?" He won't let his name be a team jersey.

He's glad he baptized hardly any of them, then, mid-letter, can't quite remember: "besides, I know not whether I baptized any other." The names were never the point. The center is Christ, crucified for them.
A neighbor tradition worries about the same split.

The Qur'an tells believers to hold fast, all together, to the rope of God, and not to break into factions. That's shared ground: a community stays one by holding the same thing, not by picking a favorite person.
And the honest difference: Paul's center is Christ, the name they were baptized into. In the Qur'an the rope is God's, and Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not as the Lord Paul names.

how: Some Christians pray for the unity of the church, and churches of different traditions sometimes gather to pray for it together.

o: a letter Paul wrote to his friend Timothy

a letter from Corinth asking Paul to visit

games.q: a church in pieces, and a neighbor's page — tap the pairs.
p: hold fast together to God's rope

s: Paul sides with the people who say 'I am of Paul'
he goes after his own fan club first: was Paul crucified for you?
Paul calls the quarreling Corinthians saints
called to be saints, in his opening lines.
warning a community not to split is found only in Christian scripture
the Qur'an tells believers to hold fast together to God's rope and not split.

games.q: a friend says the Qur'an's 'hold the rope together' proves every religion teaches the same thing. what's the fairest reply?
o: both warn against splitting; the honest difference is the center.
yes: two books warning against factions believe the same.
no: the books differ, so they share nothing at all.
games.why: shared ground is real: hold together, don't split. so is the difference: Paul's center is Christ; the Qur'an's rope is God's. neither ranks the other.

practice: Bring to mind a group you're in where people have quietly picked sides. Count three people in it you're grateful for, and make sure they aren't all from your side. Name each one, and one thing they bring.

wordCard.voice: To the church at Corinth. A letter to a quarreling church, addressed to people Paul still calls saints.

orig.note: Greek: divisions, splits. Paul's word in 1 Corinthians 1:10: that there be no divisions among you.

carryVoice: Your line: is Christ divided? Paul asks it of a church split into fan clubs, his own included. Day done.
